description: String iteration preserves supplementary characters and separate combining scalars
code:
text = "é🙂é"
seen = []
for character of text:
    seen.push(character)
assert(seen, ["é", "🙂", "e", "́"])
assert(seen.length, 4)
assert(seen.join(""), text)
seen

description: A mutated string property cannot extend a one-shot scalar snapshot
code:
holder = {text: "ab"}
seen = []
for character in holder.text:
    seen.push(character)
    holder.text = "xyz"
assert(seen, ["a", "b"])
assert(holder.text, "xyz")
holder.text = "cd"
assert(seen, ["a", "b"])
for character of holder.text:
    seen.push(character)
assert(seen, ["a", "b", "c", "d"])
seen

description: Nested named string loops restore their outer implicit iterator binding
code:
it = "outside"
letters = "xy"
digits = "12"
seen = []
for letters:
    seen.push(it)
    for digits:
        seen.push(it)
    seen.push(it)
assert(seen, ["x", "1", "2", "x", "y", "1", "2", "y"])
assert(it, "outside")
empty = ""
for empty:
    throw "UNREACHABLE"
assert(it, "outside")
seen

description: A failed scalar traversal rolls back its effects and permits a later successful loop
code:
it = "outside"
seen = ["saved"]
try:
    for it of "abc":
        seen.push(it)
        if it == "b":
            throw "CANCEL_TEXT"
catch error:
    assert(error, "CANCEL_TEXT")
assert(seen, ["saved"])
assert(it, "outside")
for it in "ok":
    seen.push(it)
assert(seen, ["saved", "o", "k"])
assert(it, "outside")
seen
